title: sapphirus.model-access-compatibility.v1
description: The reviewed compatibility policy between version one and version two of the desktop model access request. It names the single legacy profile a version one request is adapted onto, the closed set of reasons a version one request is refused, the minimum desktop contract epoch that may still speak version one, the gate that must be satisfied before version one is removed, and the guarantee that receipts signed before version two landed stay verifiable. The adapter is one way: a version one request is lifted to version two, and a version two request is never lowered.

acceptedRequestSchemaVersions.description: Request document versions the support plane still accepts, oldest first. Removing version one from this list is the observable act that closes the legacy lane.

rejectionReasons.description: Every reason a version one request is refused rather than adapted. The list is closed and exhaustive, so a refusal always has a name the desktop can render.

minimumDesktopContractEpoch.description: The lowest desktop contract epoch that may still send a version one request. An installation below this epoch is refused and told to update, rather than being adapted onto the legacy profile.

LegacyRejectionReason.description: Named refusals for a version one request. A version one request may keep doing exactly what its own contract already allowed and nothing more; reaching for a version two capability is refused rather than partially honoured.

LegacyProfileBinding.description: The single named profile every adapted version one request lands on. It exists so a legacy request still has a profile identity in the version two receipt, while its deployment stays resolved server side exactly as it was before version two. The desktop never names it, never chooses it, and cannot see the deployment behind it.

HistoricalReceiptPolicy.description: Receipts signed before version two landed must keep verifying with no change to how their digest is computed. Version two adds a second receipt family; it does not restate or re-sign the first.

LegacyRemovalGate.description: What must be true before version one stops being accepted. Every condition is observable from evidence the support plane already produces, so the removal decision is not a judgement call.
